structure: Pennsylvania Code, Title 22, Chapter 4 (Academic Standards and Assessment), printed from the official Pennsylvania Code site (137 pages). Pages 1-78 are regulations (sections 4.1-4.83) and Appendices A-2 (English language arts and mathematics) and B-1 (science, environment, technology): not social studies, so backup. Appendix C (pages 79-105) holds Academic Standards for Civics and Government (strands 5.1-5.4), Geography (7.1-7.4) and History (8.1-8.4). Each is a table with one column per grade: C1 = grade 3, C2 = grade 6, C3 = grade 9, C4 = grade 12 (labeled K-3, 4-6, 7-9, 10-12). Row 1 holds the strand heading ('5.1. ...'), row 2 the grade headers ('5.1.3. GRADE 3'), row 3 a shared lead-in ('Pennsylvania's public schools shall teach...'), and the lettered statements (A., B., ...) follow with bullet descriptors and e.g. lists in the same cell. A statement can continue onto the next page in a new table with the same column. Glossaries and the Reading/Writing in History and Social Studies standards (CCSS 8.5, 8.6) are backup. Appendix C-1 (pages 106-109, Economics) and Appendix F (pages 130-136, Personal Finance) are grids: the substrand is the first column and grade bands K-2, 3-5, 6-8, 9-12 are the next four. Those pages have no text layer (they are pictures), so their text came from OCR (see issues). Appendices D (arts, health), D-1 (family and consumer sciences), E and E-1 (career education) are not social studies: backup.

issues: Scope: the upload is the whole of Chapter 4, not the separate subject PDFs used before (those files were removed). Only Appendices C (u2999-u4289), C-1 (u4290-u4509) and F (u5493-u5828) hold social studies. Everything else is labeled backup: regulations and front matter (u1-u2998), Appendices A-2 and B-1 (ELA, math, science), and Appendices D, D-1, E and E-1 (arts, health, family and consumer sciences, career education, u4510-u5492). Backup from the whole file goes to the state's PA_ALL row, not to a grade row.

Grade bands: the civics, geography and history tables have one column per grade 3, 6, 9 and 12. Following the project's PA convention (data/clean/README.md: civics, history and geography use K-3, 4-6, 7-9, 10-12), grade 3 maps to K-3, grade 6 to 4-6, grade 9 to 7-9 and grade 12 to 10-12, and each band is copied into every grade it covers. The document describes these as standards for grades 3, 6, 9 and 12, and its history introduction names the first band as grades 1-3; the K-3 label follows the convention, not the printed wording.

Shared text: the lead-in ('Pennsylvania's public schools shall teach...', row 3 of each table) and the strand headings apply to all grades (K-12). Notes that describe the standards rather than state them ('Basic concepts found in lower grades...', 'must include local-to-global progression', 'Standard Category 8.1...', the five themes, the four-statement overview and the chronology table) are examples, K-12.

Table continuations: a cell split across pages keeps its table column, so its continuation takes that column's grade (e.g. u3255, u3256, u3257). The PDF cuts a few words inside cells, so some text is garbled in the source (for example 'esources' in u3633 and 'he United States' in u3128).

Economics (Appendix C-1, pages 107-109, units u4317-u4503) and Personal Finance (Appendix F, pages 132-136, units u5527-u5817) are pictures with no text layer. Their text was read by tesseract OCR at 300 dpi (scripts/extract_units.py, ocr_units). OCR can misread words and codes (for example 'searcity' for 'scarcity', 'ch istics' for 'characteristics', and '6.1.6-3.B' for 6.1.3-5.B). Each OCR unit's grade comes from its x position: label column x=0; K-2 about x=101-104; 3-5 about x=168-173; 6-8 about x=235-249; 9-12 about x=320-339. A cell that OCR merged with a neighbour takes the column of its first word. Check these units against the PDF before the economics and personal finance text is used.

Print header and footer lines of the Pennsylvania Code web page ('10/24/26, 12:56 PM', 'Pennsylvania Code', 'about:blank', 'n/137') and the 'Final-form 22 Pa. Code ... approved ... September 12, 2024' footers are page furniture or OCR footers; they are backup, not standards.
'Intentionally blank' cells in the economics and personal finance grids are backup for their band.

Editor's notes (u4289 and u5105-u5106) say the economics standards in Appendix C expired July 1, 2026 and that Appendix C-1 applies from then, and that Appendix F (personal finance) applies from July 1, 2026. Appendix C-1 and F are the current text. Appendix E (career education) expires July 1, 2026 and is not social studies.
Reading and Writing in History and Social Studies (CCSS 8.5 and 8.6, units u4135-u4246) and the civics, geography and history glossaries are backup, following the labeling guide.
